adversarial_audit.challenge: The full scalar Hecke spectrum identifies the physical row.
adversarial_audit.response: Orthogonal rows give exactly the same scalar spectrum and all of its moments.

adversarial_audit.challenge: Adding all singular values fixes the ambiguity.
adversarial_audit.response: The singular spectrum is also independent of row orientation.

adversarial_audit.challenge: Strong Fourier sampling or arbitrary group-action observables recover the row.
adversarial_audit.response: The represented group algebra acts trivially on the multiplicity factor. Only commutant/source operations can distinguish row orientations.

adversarial_audit.challenge: The theorem rules out a PGM-specific verifier.
adversarial_audit.response: The natural PGM may constrain a_nu through its physical frame; that structure is explicitly outside this theorem.

adversarial_audit.challenge: The large orientation manifold proves a gate lower bound.
adversarial_audit.response: No circuit lower bound follows from Hilbert-space dimension.

claim_gate.reason: All commutative outcome-side data are exactly blind to the physical row orientation, and the full represented group algebra is identity on multiplicity. Only commutant or source-specific structure can support the missing verifier.

literature_links.title: On cocliques in commutative Schurian association schemes of the symmetric group

proof_obligations.resolution: Schur's lemma leaves one row vector a_nu for each live physical multiplicity block.
Direct multiplication removes a_nu because it has unit norm.
Choose orthogonal unit vectors in any multiplicity space of dimension at least two.
The group algebra is identity on physical multiplicity, while an explicit commutant projector separates the rows.
This requires the source-specific k-copy frame or polar factor and is not implied by covariance.
Outcome Hecke data are now proved insufficient; a physical source relation or observable is required.

summary: Proved that multiplicity-free outcome spectra and all singular data cannot identify the inverse-prepared physical row; the remaining route must exploit the natural PGM/source frame rather than the perfect-matching association scheme alone.

theorem.block_family: K_nu=sqrt(alpha_nu) I_(V_nu) tensor <a_nu| for arbitrary unit a_nu in the physical multiplicity space
theorem.common_output_gram: K K^*=direct_sum_nu alpha_nu I_(V_nu), independent of a_nu
theorem.common_singular_data: Each alpha_nu occurs dim(V_nu) times, so all singular values, ranks, Schatten norms, and output Hecke moments are orientation blind.
theorem.group_action_algebra_blindness: On V_nu tensor M_nu, every operator generated by the G action is in End(V_nu) tensor I_(M_nu), so all of its outcome statistics are independent of a_nu. Orientation-sensitive observables must come from the commutant or additional source structure.
theorem.natural_source_scope_limit: The theorem ranges over abstract intertwiners. It does not prove that all orientations arise from one fixed coset-state ensemble, the natural PGM, or a polynomial circuit family.
theorem.orthogonal_row_counterexample: When dim(M_nu)>=2, orthogonal a_nu and b_nu produce orthogonal inverse row states but identical output Gram data.
theorem.universal_blindness_scope: No statistic determined only by K K^*, its spherical spectrum, or singular values can recover or verify the physical row direction.

theorem_contract.data_declared_blind: K K^*, spherical eigenvalues, singular values, ranks, and unitarily invariant output moments
theorem_contract.data_not_declared_blind: source-specific physical observables, circuit dilation, PGM polar factors, and K^*K in a known physical basis
theorem_contract.outcome_representation: multiplicity-free direct sum of finite-group irreps
theorem_contract.physical_representation: same carrier irreps with arbitrary multiplicity spaces
